device.name: ROS Gazebo Gym PandaReach-v1 (Franka Panda reach, simulated)

facts.text: PandaReach-v1 is registered with entry point ros_gazebo_gym.task_envs.panda.panda_reach:PandaReachEnv and max_steps 500
The PandaReachEnv constructor defaults control_type to 'effort'
The shipped panda_reach.yaml sets load_gripper False and lists the seven panda_joint values under controlled_joints
The shipped effort bounds are -87 to 87 for panda_joint1 through panda_joint4 and -12 to 12 for panda_joint5 through panda_joint7
The action space is a Box built from the bounds of the configured control type, ordered by the action-space joints
The observation space is a Dict of observation, desired_goal and achieved_goal, each an unbounded Box shaped from a sample observation
The observation member concatenates the end-effector position with the finger joint positions and velocities selected by the panda_finger name
The shipped panda_reach.yaml selects the dense reward type
The non-sparse reward subtracts the goal distance and any enabled collision penalty, then uses its absolute value when positive_reward is true
The episode terminates when the goal distance is below distance_threshold, and with target_hold it requires hold_samples consecutive samples
The shipped config sets target_hold True, hold_samples 2 and distance_threshold 0.05
A global target is drawn uniformly from the target sampling bounds of the environment's numpy generator
The shipped global target bounds are x 0.1 to 0.8, y -0.4 to 0.4 and z 0.1 to 1.0
The info dictionary returns reference, state_of_interest and reference_error
reset() calls the parent gymnasium reset with the seed, resets the simulation and then re-initialises the episode variables
The shipped panda_reach.yaml sets random_init_pose True
In the random end-effector sampling branch, reset calls _get_random_ee_pose when first-episode randomization is enabled or episode_num is not zero
The shipped config pauses the simulation after every step
The shipped config selects the ODE physics engine
The upstream close() calls ros_exit_gracefully with exit code 0
ros_exit_gracefully signals ROS shutdown and exits the interpreter
The environment keeps its GazeboConnection as the gazebo attribute
GAZEBO_PAUSE_PHYSICS_TOPIC is /gazebo/pause_physics
GazeboConnection's constructor creates pause_proxy, a rospy ServiceProxy of GAZEBO_PAUSE_PHYSICS_TOPIC with the std_srvs Empty type
pause_sim() calls pause_proxy in a retry loop that stops once rospy is shut down and calls ros_exit_gracefully after max_retry failures
get_physics_properties() returns the physics_properties response and raises GetPhysicsPropertiesError when its success field is false
The physics_properties property calls the get_physics_proxy service proxy
get_physics_proxy is a rospy ServiceProxy of GAZEBO_GET_PHYSICS_PROPERTIES_TOPIC with the GetPhysicsProperties type
GAZEBO_GET_PHYSICS_PROPERTIES_TOPIC is /gazebo/get_physics_properties
The environment constructor ends by unpausing the simulation
step() unpauses the simulation before it applies the action and pauses it after the observation only when pause_simulation is set
reset() pauses the simulation at its end when pause_simulation is set
PandaEnv passes pause_after_step on as pause_simulation
The shipped config sets direct_control True: arm commands are published on the controller command topics
With direct control the arm effort commands are published as Float64MultiArray on the command topic of ARM_EFFORT_CONTROLLER
ARM_EFFORT_CONTROLLER is panda_arm_joint_effort_controller
_set_action calls ros_exit_gracefully when the action shape differs from the action space shape
The constructor calls ros_exit_gracefully when a Gazebo instance is already running
ROSLauncher.initialize starts roscore in a subprocess when no ROS master is online
The constructor launches the panda_gazebo world launch file with paused set through ROSLauncher.launch
ROSLauncher.launch installs a missing launch package and its dependencies before launching it
The launch command runs in a PopenAutoCleanup subprocess through /bin/bash with shell=True
PopenAutoCleanup registers its process cleanup with atexit
The cleanup terminates the launched process's children and then the process
install_package clones a missing dependency into the workspace from the dependency index
is_repo_up_to_date fetches the repository's origin remote
Rebuilding the workspace asks whether to install the ROS system dependencies and runs sudo rosdep install only when the answer is yes
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.

determinism.notes: a seed repeats the fake's initial pose and goal, but reset preserves the source-shaped target-hold counter, so terminal results can depend on prior history; no whole-episode replay equality is claimed. Upstream additionally samples the initial pose through unseeded MoveIt

gaps: the upstream simulator was not run: it needs ROS, Gazebo, MoveIt, panda_gazebo and panda_moveit_planner_server in a catkin workspace, and this package's evidence is fake-only
the fake has no physics timestep, actuator model, sensor model or noise model; no native timing or dynamics contract has been verified; no wall-clock pacing
the initial end-effector pose is sampled through MoveIt and is not controlled by the gymnasium seed
the fake has no arm, controller, contact or sensor dynamics: it moves a 3-D end-effector position by a placeholder linear map of the first three effort components and ignores the other four
the fake is an analytic stand-in, not a recording of upstream traffic, and was never compared with a live Gazebo run

the fake draws its initial pose and goal from Python's random.Random with the shipped sampling bounds, while upstream uses numpy's generator and MoveIt, so one seed gives different episodes on the two
the fake does not model controller waits, collisions, the gripper or rendering; the shipped collision_penalty is 0.0 and the shipped config loads no gripper
no snapshot/restore is offered and step() declares no fixed simulated duration

the fake models only the pause state of /gazebo/pause_physics and get_physics_properties; that the real services set and report the world's paused flag is cited from the companion gazebo_ros 2.9.3, while what a paused Gazebo world still runs is Gazebo classic's and is not shown by the fake
reset retains the target-hold counter, matching panda_reach.py:1793-1800; an interrupted or truncated episode with one held sample can change the next episode's terminal result despite the same seed
a running step or reset is never interrupted: the e-stop pauses the world, waits for the call and pauses again; a step that outlives its bound stays owned and blocks safety reset until it answers

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the Gazebo world paused by /gazebo/pause_physics in the isolated host and confirmed by get_physics_properties pause True; the endpoint latch and the host fence refuse every step and reset; the controllers keep their last effort command, which acts again when a later step unpauses the world; another ROS client or the Gazebo GUI can unpause it. A host that is dead, unresponsive or not confirming is SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED
